title: Resolving positive semi-definiteness in physics-informed kernels for scientific machine learning
summary: Many modern machine learning models can be understood as kernel-based function-space models, including Gaussian processes and neural tangent kernels. In scientific machine learning, differential operators are increasingly used to encode physical structure directly into such models. However, it has remained unclear under which conditions these constructions are valid machine learning models, i.e. preserve positive semi-definiteness, and whether observed instabilities arise from ill-posed modeling or numerical effects. Here, we establish a simple and sufficient condition for positive semi-definiteness: for linear differential operators of order m, the base kernel must be m-times continuously differentiable. Crucially, this guarantee holds for operators with non-constant and even discontinuous coefficients. Examples are ubiquitous in physical systems, including diffusion, material elasticity, wave propagation in inhomogeneous media, and quantum systems. We conclude that remaining instabilities are attributable to numerical issues, providing a unifying validity foundation for operator-informed kernel methods.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a simple sufficient condition for positive semi-definiteness in operator-informed kernel methods: for linear differential operators of order m, the base kernel must be m-times continuously differentiable. This guarantee holds even for operators with non-constant or discontinuous coefficients, proving that these constructions are valid machine learning models and that remaining instabilities are numerical rather than ill-posed modeling issues.
AI.motivation: While differential operators are increasingly used to encode physical structure into kernel-based models (e.g., Gaussian processes, neural tangent kernels), it has remained unclear under what conditions these constructions preserve positive semi-definiteness and thus constitute valid machine learning models. The authors aim to resolve whether observed instabilities arise from ill-posed modeling or numerical effects.
AI.method: The authors derive and prove a sufficient condition for positive semi-definiteness of operator-informed kernels: for linear differential operators of order m, the base kernel must be m-times continuously differentiable. They demonstrate that this guarantee extends to operators with non-constant and even discontinuous coefficients.
AI.result: The paper proves that m-times continuous differentiability of the base kernel suffices for positive semi-definiteness under linear differential operators of order m, robust even with non-constant or discontinuous coefficients. This covers diverse physical systems including diffusion, material elasticity, wave propagation in inhomogeneous media, and quantum systems.
AI.conclusion: The authors conclude that remaining instabilities in operator-informed kernel methods are attributable to numerical issues, not theoretical invalidity, providing a unifying validity foundation for operator-informed kernel methods in scientific machine learning.

title: Symmetry Adapted Hierarchical Equations of Motion for Exact Simulations of Large Polariton Systems
summary: Hierarchical equations of motion(HEOM) provide exact dynamics of open quantum systems coupled to harmonic baths, but their computational cost becomes prohibitive for systems with many independent local environments. In this work, we develop a symmetry-adapted HEOM formalism to significantly reduce the computational cost for the permutationally invariant Holstein-Tavis-Cummings (HTC) model. The method removes redundant information in two stages. First, all auxiliary density operators (ADOs) related only by relabeling identical molecules and their bath channels are replaced by a single canonical occupation-pattern representative. Second, molecules with the same local hierarchy occupation produce repeated matrix elements within each representative, allowing only the distinct complex variables to be propagated instead of the full (N + 1) $\times$ (N + 1) ADO matrices. The resulting matrix-free equations are evaluated using precomputed connections and molecular multiplicities. At fixed hierarchy depth L and number of bath correlation exponentials m, the number of canonical representatives becomes independent of the ensemble size for N $\geq$ L and the number of unique variables saturates for N $\geq$ L + 2. The formulation easily extends to multiple-exponential bath decompositions, arbitrary initial density operators, static disorders, and cavity loss. Our benchmarks reproduce conventional HEOM dynamics while requiring far fewer propagated variables and substantially less memory.

AI.tldr: A symmetry-adapted hierarchical equations of motion (HEOM) formalism is developed for the permutationally invariant Holstein-Tavis-Cummings model, reducing computational cost by grouping equivalent auxiliary density operators and propagating only distinct matrix variables, with the number of canonical representatives becoming independent of ensemble size at fixed hierarchy depth.
AI.motivation: Standard HEOM provides exact open quantum system dynamics but becomes prohibitively expensive for systems with many independent local environments, particularly for many-molecule systems coupled to individual baths. The paper aims to reduce this computational bottleneck by exploiting permutation symmetry in the Holstein-Tavis-Cummings model.
AI.method: The method removes redundancy in two stages: (1) all auxiliary density operators (ADOs) related by relabeling identical molecules and bath channels are collapsed into a single canonical occupation-pattern representative; (2) molecules sharing the same local hierarchy occupation yield repeated matrix elements within each representative, allowing only distinct complex variables to be propagated in a matrix-free fashion. Precomputed connections and molecular multiplicities are used, with extensions to multiple-exponential baths, arbitrary initial states, static disorder, and cavity loss.
AI.result: At fixed hierarchy depth L and number of bath correlation exponentials m, the number of canonical representatives is independent of ensemble size for N ≥ L, and the number of unique variables saturates for N ≥ L + 2. Benchmarks reproduce conventional HEOM dynamics while requiring far fewer propagated variables and substantially less memory.
AI.conclusion: The symmetry-adapted HEOM formalism significantly reduces computational cost and memory requirements for the permutationally invariant HTC model while preserving exact dynamics, making it feasible to study large molecular ensembles coupled to local baths.

title: Scalable photoexcitation-induced molecular dynamics with machine-learned Hamiltonians
summary: Ultrafast photoexcitation offers a controllable route to steer structural dynamics in solids, yet predicting how nonequilibrium electronic excitation drives lattice motion across extended spatial and temporal scales remains a major computational challenge. Here we introduce time-dependent ab-initio propagation with electronic machine learning (TDAP-eML), a framework that explicitly incorporates electronic evolution into scalable simulations of photoexcitation-induced lattice dynamics. By integrating machine-learned electronic structure with atomistic propagation, TDAP-eML describes how photoexcitation reshapes the evolving energy landscapes and forces governing structural motion. Across representative examples including silicon and FeSe, the framework reproduces key photoexcited lattice responses obtained from first-principles time-dependent density functional theory calculations and captures coherent phonon dynamics together with their dependence on excitation conditions. Its computational advantage increases with system size, reaching nearly three orders of magnitude reduction in computational cost for the large systems examined. TDAP-eML thus establishes a scalable framework for coupled electronic and lattice evolution, linking nonequilibrium excitation to photoinduced forces, predictive structural dynamics, and experimentally accessible observables.

AI.tldr: Introduces TDAP-eML, a framework combining time-dependent ab-initio propagation with electronic machine learning to enable scalable simulations of photoexcitation-induced lattice dynamics, achieving up to ~1000x computational speedup while reproducing first-principles TDDFT results in silicon and FeSe.
AI.motivation: Predicting how nonequilibrium electronic excitation drives lattice motion across extended spatial and temporal scales is a major computational challenge, limiting the ability to control structural dynamics in solids via ultrafast photoexcitation.
AI.method: Integrates machine-learned electronic structure with atomistic propagation within a time-dependent ab-initio framework, explicitly incorporating electronic evolution to compute how photoexcitation reshapes energy landscapes and forces governing structural motion.
AI.result: Reproduces key photoexcited lattice responses from first-principles TDDFT in silicon and FeSe, captures coherent phonon dynamics and their dependence on excitation conditions, and achieves nearly three orders of magnitude reduction in computational cost for large systems.
AI.conclusion: TDAP-eML establishes a scalable framework for coupled electronic and lattice evolution, linking nonequilibrium excitation to photoinduced forces, predictive structural dynamics, and experimentally accessible observables.

title: On Transmission Function Amplitude and Phase Recovery in Multislice Electron Ptychography
summary: {Multislice electron ptychography commonly accounts for inelastic scattering by including an absorptive object potential in the reconstruction forward model that attenuates the elastic signal. However, it remains unclear how the reconstruction is quantitatively impacted by thermal scattering. Here, we use the quantum excitation of phonons (QEP) formalism, which explicitly separates elastic and inelastic (thermal diffuse) scattering within a single multislice propagation, to simulate four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D STEM) datasets of PbTiO$_3$ and SrTiO$_3$ and reconstruct their phase and amplitude. We find that reconstructions of the QEP total and elastic-only datasets are nearly indistinguishable across sample thicknesses from 11 to 40 nm and across atomic species, demonstrating that the reconstruction is largely insensitive to incoherent thermal diffuse scattering within the collected angular range. Reconstructions from multislice phase-only simulations further confirm that appreciable amplitude does not arise from multiple elastic scattering, but instead reflects attenuation of the coherent elastic signal due to thermal scattering. Further comparison of the QEP elastic-only reconstruction with absorptive multislice simulations reveals substantial amplitude contrast deviations for heavy Pb columns (up to 17\%), arising from the approximations used to evaluate the absorptive potential for the 4D STEM simulation. These results thus indicate that reconstruction phase and amplitude accuracy are not significantly limited by the absorptive potential forward model, even in the presence of thermal diffuse scattering.

AI.tldr: This paper systematically investigates how thermal diffuse scattering affects multislice electron ptychography reconstructions. Using the quantum excitation of phonons (QEP) formalism, the authors simulate 4D STEM datasets of PbTiO3 and SrTiO3 and find that reconstructions from QEP total and elastic-only datasets are nearly indistinguishable across thicknesses of 11–40 nm. However, absorptive potential approximations cause substantial amplitude contrast deviations (up to 17%) for heavy Pb columns.
AI.motivation: Multislice electron ptychography typically accounts for inelastic scattering using an absorptive object potential, but it remains unclear how thermal scattering quantitatively impacts the reconstruction. This uncertainty limits confidence in the accuracy of reconstructed phase and amplitude maps.
AI.method: The authors use the quantum excitation of phonons (QEP) formalism, which explicitly separates elastic and inelastic (thermal diffuse) scattering within a single multislice propagation, to simulate 4D STEM datasets of PbTiO3 and SrTiO3. They also perform multislice phase-only simulations and absorptive multislice simulations for comparison.
AI.result: Reconstructions from QEP total and elastic-only datasets are nearly indistinguishable across thicknesses from 11–40 nm and across atomic species. Phase-only simulations confirm that amplitude arises from thermal diffuse scattering attenuation rather than multiple elastic scattering. Absorptive multislice simulations show substantial amplitude contrast deviations (up to 17%) for heavy Pb columns due to approximations in the absorptive potential.
AI.conclusion: Reconstruction phase and amplitude accuracy are not significantly limited by the absorptive potential forward model, even in the presence of thermal diffuse scattering. The reconstruction is largely insensitive to incoherent thermal diffuse scattering within the collected angular range.

title: Quantum critical behavior in chains of hindered dipolar planar rotors
summary: We study the ground-state properties of linear chains of dipolar planar rotors hindered by a six-fold on-site potential, a model motivated by water molecules confined in the hexagonal cavities of beryl. Using density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) calculations, we locate the quantum phase transition between the disordered and ferroelectrically ordered phases using the von Neumann entanglement entropy and the Binder ratio of the polarization. A sweep of the six-fold pinning strength shows that increasing hindrance shifts the critical dipolar coupling gc to smaller values. These results suggest that crystal-field hindrance can promote, rather than suppress, dipolar ordering. This work has implications for ferroelectricity and quantum-device tuning in confined molecular rotors

AI.tldr: This paper studies linear chains of dipolar planar rotors with a six-fold on-site potential (motivated by water molecules in beryl cavities) using DMRG. It locates the quantum phase transition between disordered and ferroelectric phases via entanglement entropy and Binder ratio, finding that stronger hindrance shifts the critical dipolar coupling to smaller values, indicating crystal-field hindrance promotes dipolar ordering.
AI.motivation: To understand how crystal-field hindrance affects dipolar ordering in confined molecular rotors, motivated by water molecules trapped in beryl's hexagonal cavities—investigating whether on-site potential suppresses or promotes ferroelectric ordering.
AI.method: Density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) calculations on linear chains of dipolar planar rotors with a six-fold on-site pinning potential. Quantum phase transition located using von Neumann entanglement entropy and Binder ratio of polarization, with sweeps over the six-fold pinning strength.
AI.result: Increasing the six-fold pinning/hindrance strength shifts the critical dipolar coupling gc to smaller values, meaning stronger crystal-field hindrance facilitates dipolar ordering rather than suppressing it.
AI.conclusion: Crystal-field hindrance can promote dipolar ordering in confined molecular rotors, with implications for ferroelectricity and quantum-device tuning in such systems.

title: Note on proliferation transitions of non-Abelian anyons
summary: We study phase transitions out of a (2+1)d topological phase driven by the proliferation of anyons in a braided fusion subcategory. We describe a general theoretical framework for such transitions, in which the topological quantum field theory (TQFT) is coupled to dynamical matter associated with anyons in the subcategory. We interpret this construction using symmetry topological field theory (SymTFT), where the dynamics is localized on the symmetry boundary of the (3+1)d slab. We analyze several examples, and present explicit Chern-Simons-Higgs (CSH) field theories realizing the proliferation transitions. We also examine proliferation transitions that implement gauging of non-invertible one-form symmetry in the parent TQFT. This includes a general construction for ${\rm Rep}(G)$ one-form symmetry for a finite group $G$, and a CSH realization of the non-invertible one-form gauging ${\rm SU}(2)_{10}\rightarrow {\rm Spin}(5)_1$. We discuss which anyons proliferate at these transitions.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a general theoretical framework for studying phase transitions out of (2+1)d topological phases driven by the proliferation of anyons in a braided fusion subcategory, using a SymTFT construction and presenting explicit Chern-Simons-Higgs field theories. It also covers proliferation transitions that implement gauging of non-invertible one-form symmetry, including Rep(G) one-form symmetry for finite groups and a CSH realization of the non-invertible gauging SU(2)_10 → Spin(5)_1.
AI.motivation: To provide a systematic and general framework for understanding anyon proliferation transitions out of (2+1)d topological phases, and to connect these to gauging of (possibly non-invertible) one-form symmetries via SymTFT and explicit Chern-Simons-Higgs constructions.
AI.method: The authors couple a TQFT to dynamical matter associated with anyons in a braided fusion subcategory, and reinterpret this via the symmetry topological field theory (SymTFT) framework where dynamics are localized on the symmetry boundary of a (3+1)d slab. They work out explicit Chern-Simons-Higgs field theory realizations for several examples, and analyze which anyons proliferate at these transitions.
AI.result: The framework yields a general description of anyon proliferation transitions, including specific CSH realizations. The authors provide a general construction for gauging Rep(G) non-invertible one-form symmetry, and a concrete CSH realization of the non-invertible gauging transition SU(2)_10 → Spin(5)_1, with a detailed discussion of which anyons proliferate.
AI.conclusion: The paper establishes a unified SymTFT-based framework for anyon proliferation transitions in (2+1)d topological phases, applicable both to ordinary and non-invertible one-form symmetry gauging, with explicit field-theoretic realizations and identification of proliferating anyons.

title: Two-dimensional percolation with algebraically decaying interactions II: Critical exponents in the long-range regime
summary: We present a comprehensive Monte Carlo study of two-dimensional bond percolation with algebraically decaying connection probabilities $p(r)\propto 1/r^{2+σ}$, establishing the universality diagram in the long-range (LR) regime for $σ\le2$. Using the event-based ensemble method, we simulate systems with linear sizes up to $L=16384$ and investigate three universality regimes: LR Wilson--Fisher (WF) A ($1<σ\le2$), LR Wilson--Fisher B ($2/3<σ\le1$), and LR mean-field (MF) ($0<σ\le2/3$). In the LR-WF-B regime, the anomalous dimension is consistent with $η=2-σ$, in agreement with mathematical results for $2/3<σ<1$, while the correlation-length exponent $ν(σ)$ exhibits nontrivial, non-Gaussian variation. In the LR-WF-A regime, although $η$ remains close to $2-σ$ for smaller $σ$, statistically resolvable deviations $δη(σ)=η-(2-σ)>0$ start to appear near $σ\simeq3/2$ and grow toward the short-range crossover at $σ=2$. Finally, by complementing the event-based simulations with conventional ensemble simulations, we reveal the coexistence of complete-graph asymptotics and LR Gaussian-fixed-point scaling in the LR-MF regime. These results further clarify the critical properties in long-range percolation and provide crucial benchmarks for long-range statistical systems.

AI.tldr: A comprehensive Monte Carlo study of two-dimensional long-range bond percolation with algebraically decaying connection probabilities, establishing the universality diagram across three regimes (LR-WF-A, LR-WF-B, LR-MF) for σ≤2 using the event-based ensemble method with system sizes up to L=16384.
AI.motivation: To establish a complete and precise universality diagram for two-dimensional long-range bond percolation, clarifying the critical properties and anomalous dimensions in regimes where theoretical predictions and numerical evidence have been incomplete or contentious.
AI.method: Event-based ensemble Monte Carlo simulations of 2D bond percolation with power-law decaying connection probabilities p(r)∝1/r^(2+σ), complemented by conventional ensemble simulations, on systems up to L=16384, covering the regimes 1<σ≤2 (LR-WF-A), 2/3<σ≤1 (LR-WF-B), and 0<σ≤2/3 (LR-MF).
AI.result: In LR-WF-B, the anomalous dimension η=2-σ agrees with mathematical results. In LR-WF-A, deviations δη>0 appear near σ≈3/2 and grow toward the short-range crossover at σ=2. In the LR-MF regime, coexistence of complete-graph asymptotics and LR Gaussian-fixed-point scaling is revealed.
AI.conclusion: The study provides a comprehensive universality diagram for long-range percolation, clarifying the anomalous dimension behavior across regimes (including nontrivial deviations in LR-WF-A) and establishing crucial numerical benchmarks for long-range statistical systems.

title: Attosecond Transient Polarimetry
summary: We introduce elliptical-dichroic attosecond transient absorption spectroscopy (eDATAS), an ultrafast attosecond spectroscopy technique in which an atomic gas is probed by elliptically polarized attosecond and near-infrared pulses with an arbitrary angle between the polarization ellipses and a varying time-delay. Using perturbation theory, we show that the transient absorption signal factorizes into form factors whose dependence on pulse ellipticities and polarization-ellipse orientations are governed entirely by dipole selection rules: ellipticity sets the amplitudes of the interfering multiphoton pathways, while the relative orientations of the ellipses control the phase. We reinterpret circular- and linear-dichroic attosecond transient absorption spectroscopy as limiting cases of eDATAS, and validate the theory through an eDATAS measurement in helium, finding excellent agreement. Finally, we demonstrate that eDATAS can also serve as an in situ measurement of the polarization state of the XUV field, avoiding the need for a dedicated XUV polarimeter.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces elliptical-dichroic attosecond transient absorption spectroscopy (eDATAS), a technique using elliptically polarized attosecond and near-infrared pulses with arbitrary relative polarization-ellipse angles and time delays. Perturbation theory shows the transient absorption signal factorizes into form factors governed by dipole selection rules, where ellipticity sets multiphoton pathway amplitudes and ellipse orientation controls phase. Linear- and circular-dichroic variants are recovered as limiting cases; the theory is validated in helium, and eDATAS also enables in situ measurement of the XUV field polarization state, replacing a dedicated XUV polarimeter.
AI.motivation: To develop a more general and flexible attosecond transient absorption spectroscopy technique that exploits elliptical polarization to access and control multiphoton interference pathways, while unifying existing linear- and circular-dichroic approaches within a single theoretical framework.
AI.method: Employing perturbation theory to derive a factorization of the transient absorption signal into form factors whose dependence on pulse ellipticities and polarization-ellipse orientations is determined entirely by dipole selection rules. The theory is then validated experimentally via an eDATAS measurement in helium.
AI.result: Excellent agreement between theory and helium eDATAS measurements; linear- and circular-dichroic ATAS are recovered as limiting cases; eDATAS provides in situ measurement of XUV polarization state, eliminating the need for a dedicated XUV polarimeter.
AI.conclusion: eDATAS is a validated, generalizable attosecond spectroscopy framework that unifies existing dichroic techniques, offers controllable multiphoton pathway interference, and provides a practical route to XUV polarimetry in situ.

title: An LLM agent for end-to-end computational materials discovery
summary: The coordination of multi-scale tasks is an effective strategy for computational materials discovery, yet the repeated application of diverse algorithms and tools renders it challenging. We report MAESTRO, a large language model (LLM) agent system capable of executing the entire screening pipeline for metal-organic frameworks (MOFs). It processes a large body of MOF literature, links relevant publications to their crystal structures, and curates the results into a computation-ready database, which is then screened through a strategy of progressively increasing computational cost. The promising candidates identified for separation under wet flue gas conditions all originate from unrelated studies. By connecting the heterogeneous stages of computational materials discovery, the LLM-based agents of MAESTRO can operate across application domains and uncover high-performance materials that conventional screening approaches would be unlikely to consider.

AI.tldr: MAESTRO is an LLM agent system that automates the entire multi-scale computational screening pipeline for metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), from literature mining and structure curation to progressively expensive computational screening, successfully identifying high-performance MOF candidates for wet flue gas separation from unrelated studies.
AI.motivation: Multi-scale task coordination is effective for computational materials discovery, but the repeated application of diverse algorithms and tools makes it challenging. There is a need to connect heterogeneous stages of the discovery pipeline to enable more comprehensive screening.
AI.method: MAESTRO employs LLM-based agents to: (1) process a large body of MOF literature, (2) link relevant publications to their crystal structures, (3) curate results into a computation-ready database, and (4) screen candidates through a strategy of progressively increasing computational cost.
AI.result: The promising candidates identified for separation under wet flue gas conditions all originate from unrelated studies, demonstrating that MAESTRO can uncover high-performance materials that conventional screening approaches would be unlikely to consider.
AI.conclusion: By connecting heterogeneous stages of computational materials discovery, LLM-based agents like MAESTRO can operate across application domains and expand the search space for high-performance materials beyond what conventional screening workflows achieve.

title: Perspectives on Magnetic/Superconductor Hybrid Systems: Long-range Electromagnetic Phenomena Induced by Proximity Effect and Interfacial Spin-orbit Coupling
comment: Published in Journal of Applied Physics, original version of the paper before copyediting, 21 pages, 16 figures
summary: In this Perspective we review recent achievements in physics and applications of hybrid superconductor-ferromagnet structures. In particular, we focus on the manifestations of the electromagnetic phenomena in these systems originating from the response of the induced superconducting correlations modified by the exchange field and additional effects coming from the interface Rashba-type spin-orbit coupling. The review includes the long-range electromagnetic proximity effect and related modification of magnetic textures, spontaneous currents, properties of vortex matter and its interaction with magnetic ordering, spin-galvanic, photogalvanic and nonreciprocal transport phenomena in exemplary hybrid systems. We also present our views on the future development of this field including both the theoretical challenges and promising opportunities for fundamental experiments.

AI.tldr: This Perspective reviews recent achievements in the physics and applications of hybrid superconductor-ferromagnet structures, focusing on electromagnetic phenomena arising from induced superconducting correlations modified by exchange fields and interface Rashba spin-orbit coupling. It covers long-range proximity effects, magnetic texture modifications, spontaneous currents, vortex matter, and various transport phenomena, concluding with future research directions.
AI.motivation: To consolidate and review recent progress in hybrid superconductor-ferromagnet systems, highlighting the electromagnetic phenomena originating from the interplay between superconducting correlations, exchange fields, and Rashba-type spin-orbit coupling at interfaces, while also outlining future theoretical challenges and experimental opportunities.
AI.method: This is a Perspective/review paper that synthesizes recent achievements in hybrid superconductor-ferromagnet structures, examining: (1) the response of induced superconducting correlations modified by exchange fields and interface Rashba-type spin-orbit coupling; (2) long-range electromagnetic proximity effects and modifications of magnetic textures; (3) spontaneous currents, vortex matter properties and their interaction with magnetic ordering; and (4) spin-galvanic, photogalvanic, and nonreciprocal transport phenomena in exemplary hybrid systems.
AI.result: The review identifies the key electromagnetic phenomena arising in superconductor-ferromagnet hybrids, including long-range proximity effects, modified magnetic textures, spontaneous currents, vortex-magnetic ordering interactions, and spin-galvanic, photogalvanic, and nonreciprocal transport effects, all influenced by exchange fields and Rashba spin-orbit coupling.
AI.conclusion: The authors present their perspective on future field development, identifying both outstanding theoretical challenges and promising experimental opportunities for fundamental studies in hybrid superconductor-ferromagnet systems.

title: Non-reciprocal heat transfer advances flexible thermoelectric devices
summary: Complex heat dissipation assemblies, inferior performance, and limited flexibility are the primary constraints impeding the wide application and commercialization of conventional flexible thermoelectric devices in wearable electronics and other high-end cooling scenarios. In this work, we report a non-conventional design for flexible thermoelectric devices which can reduce the temperature to -7.03 at room temperature without external heat sink, achieving a cooling temperature drop of 29.25. The design is based on non-reciprocal heat transfer, integrated with thermally conductive composites and screen-printing technologies. This approach takes advantage of directional heat flow, thereby eliminating the need for complex heat sink networks, which extend the applications of flexible thermoelectric devices from personal thermal management to more broader fields such as home healthcare and emergency first aid.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a non-conventional flexible thermoelectric device design based on non-reciprocal heat transfer that achieves a cooling temperature drop of 29.25°C (reaching -7.03°C at room temperature) without an external heat sink, using thermally conductive composites and screen-printing technologies.
AI.motivation: Conventional flexible thermoelectric devices suffer from complex heat dissipation assemblies, inferior performance, and limited flexibility, which hinder their application in wearable electronics and high-end cooling scenarios. The need for external heat sinks is a major barrier to commercialization.
AI.method: The design leverages non-reciprocal heat transfer to achieve directional heat flow, integrated with thermally conductive composites and screen-printing technologies, thereby eliminating the need for complex heat sink networks.
AI.result: The device achieves a cooling temperature of -7.03°C at room temperature without an external heat sink, corresponding to a cooling temperature drop of 29.25°C.
AI.conclusion: This approach extends the applications of flexible thermoelectric devices beyond personal thermal management to broader fields such as home healthcare and emergency first aid, by overcoming heat dissipation and flexibility constraints.

title: Real-time ESR tracking for sub-micron 3D magnetic mapping with VB- quantum sensors in hexagonal boron nitride
summary: The discovery of spin-dependent luminescent properties of negatively charged boron-vacancy centers ($V^-_B$) in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) enabled a new platform for quantum sensing with van der Waals materials. Particularly, the possibility of performing optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) for determining the electron spin resonance (ESR) frequencies of hBN color centers became a strong tool for quantum sensing of magnetic fields with submicrometric resolution. However, due to low ODMR contrast, current techniques proposed for mapping DC magnetic fields require hours of integration to obtain a magnetic image of a micron-sized region. In this work, we report the implementation of a frequency-tracking approach for real-time monitoring of ESR frequencies of localized $V^-_B$ centers in hBN. With this technique, magnetic field monitoring was used to map the field pattern generated by a micron-sized conical magnetic tip in only a few minutes. By controlling the magnetic sample's position relative to the quantum sensor, three-dimensional magnetic mapping of the field was achieved with diffraction-limited resolution and shot-noise-limited sensitivity of 54 $μ$T$/\sqrt{\text{Hz}}$. Magnetic field gradients of 3.6 $\pm$ 0.2 $μ$T/nm were measured with our system, in which a maximum detected field rate of 6 mT/s was achieved. The results of this study establish spin resonance frequency-tracking as a viable technique and fast method for minute-scale magnetic imaging, reducing acquisition times by at least one order of magnitude if compared to conventional techniques.

AI.tldr: The paper reports a frequency-tracking approach for real-time monitoring of electron spin resonance frequencies of negatively charged boron-vacancy (V_B^-) centers in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN), enabling fast three-dimensional magnetic field mapping of a conical magnetic tip with diffraction-limited resolution and shot-noise-limited sensitivity of 54 μT/√Hz. This method reduces imaging acquisition times by at least one order of magnitude compared to conventional ODMR-based techniques.
AI.motivation: Conventional ODMR-based magnetic imaging techniques using V_B^- centers in hBN suffer from low ODMR contrast, requiring hours of integration to produce a magnetic image of a micron-sized region. The authors aim to develop a faster method for DC magnetic field mapping with submicrometric resolution.
AI.method: The authors implement a frequency-tracking approach for real-time monitoring of ESR frequencies of localized V_B^- color centers in hBN. By controlling the position of the magnetic sample relative to the quantum sensor, they achieve three-dimensional magnetic field mapping.
AI.result: Three-dimensional magnetic mapping was achieved with diffraction-limited resolution and shot-noise-limited sensitivity of 54 μT/√Hz. Magnetic field gradients of 3.6 ± 0.2 μT/nm were measured, with a maximum detected field rate of 6 mT/s. Imaging was completed in a few minutes, reducing acquisition times by at least one order of magnitude.
AI.conclusion: Spin resonance frequency-tracking is established as a viable and fast technique for minute-scale magnetic imaging using hBN quantum sensors, significantly outperforming conventional ODMR-based approaches in acquisition speed.

title: Shaping liquids into space structures - microgravity-assisted design and manufacturing of minimal surfaces
summary: This work advances a fundamentally new approach to space-based construction by using liquid self organization in microgravity as a generative design and fabrication principle. Building on the LiquiFab method, we demonstrate how minimal surface architectures - traditionally dependent on complex additive manufacturing - can instead emerge directly from the physics of fluid interfaces shaped by programmable boundary conditions. We present a simulation-to-fabrication workflow, that includes a boundary-driven minimal-surface solver integrated in Grasshopper/Rhino, and an experimental system that implements in a neutral buoyancy environment simulating microgravity. This enables the generation of customizable Schwarz-P-inspired with tunable geometry and thickness, illustrating a scalable pathway for material-efficient, on-orbit fabrication. To validate performance in true microgravity, a flight experiment on the International Space Station is scheduled for the first quarter of 2027 and we here detail the additional considerations required for this experiment.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a new approach to space-based construction using liquid self-organization in microgravity, where minimal surface architectures emerge directly from fluid physics rather than additive manufacturing. The authors demonstrate a simulation-to-fabrication workflow including a boundary-driven minimal-surface solver in Grasshopper/Rhino and an experimental system in neutral buoyancy. They generate customizable Schwarz-P-inspired geometries with tunable properties, and detail plans for a flight experiment on the ISS scheduled for Q1 2027.
AI.motivation: Traditional space-based construction relies on complex additive manufacturing, which is inefficient and difficult to deploy on-orbit. The authors seek a fundamentally new generative design approach that exploits liquid self-organization in microgravity to create structural architectures from fluid physics, offering a more material-efficient and scalable path for on-orbit fabrication.
AI.method: The work extends the LiquiFab method, using programmable boundary conditions to shape fluid interfaces into minimal surface architectures. It includes: (1) a boundary-driven minimal-surface solver integrated into Grasshopper/Rhino for simulation, and (2) an experimental system operating in a neutral buoyancy environment to simulate microgravity, enabling fabrication of customizable Schwarz-P-inspired structures with tunable geometry and thickness.
AI.result: The simulation-to-fabrication workflow successfully generates tunable Schwarz-P-inspired minimal surface architectures without additive manufacturing. Validation in neutral buoyancy demonstrates feasibility, and a flight experiment aboard the International Space Station is scheduled for Q1 2027 to confirm performance in true microgravity, with additional experimental considerations detailed.
AI.conclusion: Liquid self-organization is a viable generative design and fabrication principle for space-based construction, offering a scalable, material-efficient alternative to additive manufacturing. The scheduled ISS flight experiment will provide the critical microgravity validation needed to confirm the approach's on-orbit applicability.

title: $\mathcal{PT}$ and anti-$\mathcal{PT}$ phase transitions in a trimerized Su--Schrieffer--Heeger chain with nonreciprocal Rashba spin-orbit coupling
summary: We theoretically investigate a one-dimensional trimerized Su--Schrieffer--Heeger chain with three sublattices per unit cell subjected to a nonreciprocal Rashba spin-orbit coupling. Invoking a spin-flip symmetry, the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian decomposes into two independent spin sectors, enabling a spin-resolved analysis of non-Hermitian skin effects and system symmetries. We identify a rich phase diagram consisting of four bulk phases and two edge-state phases. The bulk phases include fully $\mathcal{PT}$-unbroken (real-spectrum) and fully anti-$\mathcal{PT}$-unbroken (imaginary-spectrum) regimes, as well as two mixed phases where one band remains on the real or imaginary axis while the other two form complex-conjugate pairs. The two edge-state phases correspond to topological edge modes with either $\mathcal{PT}$-unbroken (real) or anti-$\mathcal{PT}$-unbroken (imaginary) energies. Using non-Bloch band theory and Cardano's method, we derive closed-form expressions for phase boundaries and establish the bulk-edge correspondence for each spin sector. Calculations of Berry phase and directional inverse participation ratios confirm our analytical predictions. Our results provide a minimal platform for realizing spin-resolved non-Hermitian topology and edge-selective symmetry preservation, in which the bulk and edge states belong to distinct symmetry classes.

Using spin-flip symmetry, the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian decomposes into independent spin sectors, revealing a phase diagram with four bulk phases (fully PT-unbroken, fully anti-PT-unbroken, and two mixed phases) and two edge-state phases. Non-Bloch band theory and Cardano's method provide closed-form phase boundaries and establish bulk-edge correspondence, confirmed by Berry phase and directional inverse participation ratio calculations.
AI.motivation: To understand and realize spin-resolved non-Hermitian topology where bulk and edge states belong to distinct symmetry classes, providing a minimal platform for spin-dependent non-Hermitian physics beyond conventional PT-symmetric systems.
AI.method: The system is a trimerized SSH chain with nonreciprocal Rashba spin-orbit coupling, decomposed into two spin sectors via spin-flip symmetry. Non-Bloch band theory, Cardano's method for closed-form phase boundaries, plus Berry phase and directional inverse participation ratio calculations are employed.

Closed-form expressions for phase boundaries are derived, and bulk-edge correspondence is established for each spin sector, validated by Berry phase and directional IPR calculations.

title: Distinguishing Mott and strain-induced anisotropic semimetals in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene using Landau level spectroscopy
summary: Recent quantum twisting microscopy experiments [1] have provided unprecedented momentum- and energy-resolved imaging of magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, revealing a stark dichotomy between the heavy and light electronic characters of its narrow bands. In this work, we provide a sharp distinguishing criterion between the two most likely candidate states that exhibit spectroscopic features consistent with the experimental results. Focusing on charge neutrality, these states are 1) the 'Mott semimetal', governed by strong dynamical correlations, and 2) the 'strain-induced anisotropic semimetal', characterized by weak Hartree-Fock effects. We demonstrate that an out-of- plane magnetic field serves as a sharp discriminating probe based on the expected Landau level gap size hierarchy. We find that the strain-induced anisotropic semimetal has a robust gap hierarchy where the Chern C gaps, Δ_C , decrease in order Δ_{\pm 4} > Δ_{\pm 8} > Δ_{\pm 12}. In contrast, for the Mott semimetal, Δ_{\pm 4} remains the largest gap, while the relative magnitude of the C = \pm 8, \pm 12 gaps depends sensitively on the applied magnetic field. We test the robustness of these results against strain orientation and lattice relaxation finding consistency between the gap hierarchy of the strained semimetal and previous incompressibility measurements at finite magnetic field [2].

AI.tldr: The paper provides a sharp criterion to distinguish between two candidate states of magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene at charge neutrality—the "Mott semimetal" and the "strain-induced anisotropic semimetal"—using an out-of-plane magnetic field as a discriminating probe based on the hierarchy of Landau level (Chern gap) sizes. The strained semimetal exhibits a robust gap hierarchy Δ±4 > Δ±8 > Δ±12, whereas the Mott semimetal shows a field-dependent relative magnitude for the ±8 and ±12 gaps.
AI.motivation: Quantum twisting microscopy experiments have revealed a stark dichotomy between heavy and light electronic characters in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene narrow bands. Since multiple candidate states produce consistent spectroscopic features, a sharp distinguishing criterion is needed to determine which state actually governs the physics at charge neutrality.
AI.method: The authors compare two candidate states—the Mott semimetal (strong dynamical correlations) and the strain-induced anisotropic semimetal (weak Hartree-Fock effects)—and analyze their Landau level gap hierarchies under an out-of-plane magnetic field. They test the robustness of results against strain orientation and lattice relaxation, comparing against previous incompressibility measurements at finite magnetic field.
AI.result: The strain-induced anisotropic semimetal has a robust gap hierarchy with Chern gaps decreasing as Δ±4 > Δ±8 > Δ±12. In contrast, for the Mott semimetal, Δ±4 remains the largest gap but the relative magnitudes of C=±8 and ±12 gaps depend sensitively on the applied magnetic field. The strained semimetal's gap hierarchy is consistent with previous incompressibility measurements at finite magnetic field.
AI.conclusion: An out-of-plane magnetic field serves as a sharp discriminating probe between the two candidate states at charge neutrality in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, based on their distinct Landau level gap hierarchies. The strain-induced anisotropic semimetal is consistent with existing finite-field experimental measurements.

title: Quantum Wake Dynamics from Distinct Spectroscopic Perturbations
summary: Quantum wake dynamics in quantum magnets have recently been inferred from the dynamical spin structure factor, which probes only a restricted class of local perturbations. Here, we show that resonant inelastic x-ray scattering (RIXS) selection rules act as an operator filter on fractionalized excitations, producing distinct quantum wakes in the spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ Heisenberg antiferromagnetic chain. Using explicit real-time evolution of single-spin and spin-conserving bond correlators, we find that the conventional spin response propagates up to the maximum spinon velocity, $v_s=\fracπ{2} J$, whereas the bond channels concentrate their spectral weight into a slower dominant wake with $v\simeq 0.92 J$, while weaker components remain bounded by the full spinon light cone. The corresponding momentum- and frequency-resolved responses map onto experimentally accessible RIXS channels, demonstrating that different spectroscopic perturbations resolve complementary pathways of many-body propagation beyond the neutron-scattering spin structure factor. Their inelastic spectral weights further provide access to quantum Fisher information, while equal-time bond sum rules connect the same spectroscopic channels to the ground-state energy. Because the same correlators can be prepared and measured on quantum hardware, they also define direct, experimentally anchored benchmarks for quantum simulations, particularly in frustrated and higher-dimensional magnets where controlled classical real-time calculations become challenging.

There is a need to understand how different spectroscopic probes beyond neutron scattering can resolve complementary pathways of many-body propagation in fractionalized spin systems.
AI.method: The authors perform explicit real-time evolution of single-spin and spin-conserving bond correlators in the spin-1/2 Heisenberg antiferromagnetic chain. They analyze RIXS selection rules as an operator filter on fractionalized excitations and compute momentum- and frequency-resolved responses mapped onto experimentally accessible RIXS channels.

The inelastic spectral weights provide access to quantum Fisher information, and equal-time bond sum rules connect spectroscopic channels to ground-state energy.
AI.conclusion: Different spectroscopic perturbations resolve complementary pathways of many-body propagation beyond the neutron-scattering spin structure factor. The same correlators can be prepared and measured on quantum hardware, making them direct benchmarks for quantum simulations, especially in frustrated and higher-dimensional magnets where classical real-time calculations face challenges.

title: Magic Velocity Selection in Atom Interferometry
summary: Velocity-selective Raman transitions are widely used in atom interferometers to prepare atomic ensembles with narrowly defined momentum distributions. However, differential light shifts between atomic energy levels generate velocity distributions that are correlated with the Raman beam intensity, and therefore with the position of the atoms within the laser beam. We show that these spatially inhomogeneous velocity distributions interact with detuning-dependent systematic effects in a Bragg diffraction-based simultaneous conjugate Ramsey-Bordé interferometer. These interactions can induce systematic phase shifts of order 10 milliradians in the interferometer phase. We further identify a "magic" detuning for velocity selection and show that operating at this detuning suppresses the systematic phase shift. Magic velocity selection eliminates systematic errors arising from correlations between atom velocity and position, facilitating high-resolution atom interferometry experiments targeting sub-part-per-billion accuracy.

AI.tldr: Velocity-selective Raman transitions in atom interferometers create velocity distributions correlated with laser intensity and atomic position, which interact with detuning-dependent systematics in Bragg-based conjugate Ramsey-Bordé interferometers, inducing ~10 mrad phase shifts. A "magic" detuning suppresses this effect, enabling sub-part-per-billion accuracy.
AI.motivation: Velocity-selective Raman transitions generate spatially inhomogeneous velocity distributions due to differential light shifts correlated with beam intensity. These distributions can cause systematic phase errors in high-precision atom interferometry, limiting accuracy at the sub-part-per-billion level.
AI.method: The authors analyze how spatially inhomogeneous velocity distributions produced by Raman velocity selection couple with detuning-dependent systematics in a Bragg diffraction-based simultaneous conjugate Ramsey-Bordé interferometer. They derive the resulting phase shifts and identify a "magic" detuning for velocity selection that cancels these systematic effects.
AI.result: The interaction between position-correlated velocity distributions and detuning-dependent systematics induces systematic phase shifts on the order of 10 milliradians. Operating at the identified "magic" detuning suppresses these systematic phase shifts.
AI.conclusion: Magic velocity selection eliminates systematic errors arising from velocity-position correlations, facilitating high-resolution atom interferometry experiments targeting sub-part-per-billion accuracy.

title: Carrier Capture at Defects from Finite-Temperature Lattice Dynamics
summary: Defect-assisted carrier capture is commonly described within nonradiative multiphonon (NMP) theory using normal modes of the equilibrium defect structure. This description becomes inadequate when finite-temperature lattice fluctuations explore configurations that cannot be represented by a fixed normal-mode basis. Here, we present a trajectory-based method for calculating carrier capture rate from first principles, which allows lattice relaxation and electron--lattice coupling matrix element to be reconstructed directly from correlation functions of finite-temperature lattice dynamics. For hole capture at C$_\mathrm{N}$ in GaN within harmonic regime, the method reproduces static NMP results including mode mixing and agrees with experiment. For oxygen vacancy in SiO$_2$, by contrast, the thermally sampled potential energy surface is substantially softer than the zero-temperature normal-mode harmonic expansion, strongly modifying the lattice relaxation and electron--lattice coupling, and producing pronounced changes in both the capture coefficient and its temperature dependence. These results establish the finite-temperature configurational ensemble, rather than phonon occupations alone, as an essential ingredient of defect-assisted carrier capture.

AI.tldr: A trajectory-based first-principles method for calculating carrier capture rates that reconstructs lattice relaxation and electron-lattice coupling from finite-temperature correlation functions, demonstrating that finite-temperature configurational sampling (not just phonon occupations) is essential for accurate defect-assisted capture rates.
AI.motivation: Standard nonradiative multiphonon (NMP) theory uses normal modes of the equilibrium defect structure, which fails when finite-temperature lattice fluctuations explore configurations not representable by a fixed normal-mode basis.
AI.method: A trajectory-based method that computes carrier capture rates from first principles by reconstructing lattice relaxation and electron-lattice coupling matrix elements directly from correlation functions of finite-temperature lattice dynamics.
AI.result: For hole capture at CN in GaN, the method reproduces static NMP results including mode mixing and agrees with experiment. For oxygen vacancy in SiO2, the thermally sampled potential energy surface is substantially softer than the zero-temperature harmonic expansion, strongly modifying lattice relaxation and electron-lattice coupling, leading to pronounced changes in both capture coefficient and its temperature dependence.
AI.conclusion: The finite-temperature configurational ensemble, rather than phonon occupations alone, is an essential ingredient of defect-assisted carrier capture.

title: A non-local power-law baseline for transient flux penetration in YBCO films: parameter degeneracy and constitutive limitations
summary: We assess whether a non-local thin-film model with a bounded, constant-exponent power law can reproduce high-speed magneto-optical measurements of transient flux penetration in a $3\times3$~mm$^2$ YBa$_2$Cu$_3$O$_{7-δ}$ film. The model is solved forward in physical units and used as a controlled constitutive baseline. The critical sheet current is constrained by the final penetration geometry, while the criterion field and creep exponent are constrained by the turnover and relaxation times. The calibration reveals an intrinsic degeneracy: the turnover time depends primarily on the product of the criterion field and saturation parameter, equivalently on the saturated sheet resistivity, so these quantities cannot be identified independently. After parameterizing this degeneracy, the model captures a guarded-current turnover near 22~ms, a relaxation constant of 41.2~ms compared with the measured 37.5 and 43.7~ms, and a late maximum approximately 0.92~mm from the film edge. The amplitude remains discrepant: the calculated transient maximum is $1.90J_{c0}$ and the peak-to-225-ms ratio is 2.13, compared with the reported 1.20. This excess persists under changes in the creep exponent, the degenerate parameter direction, the Kim field dependence, and mesh resolution. Matching the measured ratio through the criterion field would require a value about three orders of magnitude below the conventional scale, while spatial exclusion sufficient to match it would remove the edge peak itself. We also decompose the electric field into irrotational and solenoidal parts and quantify the boundary layer where spectral and finite-difference forms of Faraday's law disagree. The results establish a reproducible non-local power-law baseline and identify limitations of the bounded, constant-exponent constitutive family rather than of non-local thin-film electrodynamics.

AI.tldr: The paper assesses a non-local thin-film model with a bounded, constant-exponent power law against high-speed magneto-optical measurements of transient flux penetration in a YBa₂Cu₃O₇₋δ film. Calibration reveals an intrinsic degeneracy between criterion field and saturation parameter, and while the model captures turnover and relaxation times, it fails to match the measured transient amplitude—an excess that persists across parameter and numerical variations, indicating limitations of the constitutive family rather than non-local electrodynamics.
AI.motivation: To determine whether a non-local thin-film model with a bounded, constant-exponent power law can reproduce high-speed magneto-optical measurements of transient flux penetration, and to identify whether discrepancies arise from the constitutive model or from the non-local electrodynamic framework itself.
AI.method: The model is solved forward in physical units and used as a controlled constitutive baseline. Critical sheet current is constrained by final penetration geometry; criterion field and creep exponent are constrained by turnover and relaxation times. A degeneracy analysis parameterizes the product of criterion field and saturation parameter (saturated sheet resistivity). However, the calculated transient maximum is 1.90Jc0 with a peak-to-225-ms ratio of 2.13 versus the reported 1.20. Matching the measured ratio would require a criterion field three orders of magnitude below conventional scale, while spatial exclusion sufficient to match it would remove the edge peak itself. The excess persists under variations in creep exponent, degenerate parameter direction, Kim field dependence, and mesh resolution.
AI.conclusion: The bounded, constant-exponent constitutive family is insufficient to reproduce the measured transient amplitude, establishing a reproducible non-local power-law baseline and pointing to limitations of the constitutive family rather than of non-local thin-film electrodynamics.

title: Electrostatic Influence of Diamond Heat-Spreaders on GaN FET Performance
summary: Diamond, with its exceptional thermal conductivity, is widely explored as a heat spreader to improve thermal management in GaN-based power and RF electronics. In this work, we use Sentaurus TCAD to model AlGaN/GaN HEMTs with integrated diamond heat spreaders, incorporating advanced physical models such as thermal boundary resistance (TBR) and temperature-dependent bandgap narrowing. While diamond significantly enhances heat dissipation, our simulations reveal an important but often overlooked tradeoff: electrostatic modulation at the diamond and semiconductor interface. We initially modeled a p-GaN HEMT with all-around diamond integration and show agreement to the experimentally reported electrothermal benefits of diamond heat spreader integration. However, we observe strong band bending at the diamond/GaN interface alongside electric field generation and increased valence band energy in diamond. As a result, an interfacial hole accumulation region forms at the GaN surface, altering vertical transport and hindering current injection which prevents high on-state current. These results indicate that although diamond improves thermal performance, it can also actively influence the electrostatics of the transistor. To address both the elevated TBR and the undesired interfacial band bending, we propose the incorporation of an engineered interlayer. Building on our Sentaurus TCAD results, we develop a Silvaco TCAD TLM test structure to characterize the extent of the hole accumulation region formation and give insight to future studies on mitigation through interlayer development.

AI.tldr: This work uses Sentaurus TCAD and Silvaco TCAD to model AlGaN/GaN HEMTs with integrated diamond heat spreaders, revealing a tradeoff between improved thermal dissipation and electrostatic degradation at the diamond/GaN interface. The simulation shows that while diamond enhances heat spreading, it induces band bending and hole accumulation at the GaN surface, hindering current injection and on-state performance. An engineered interlayer is proposed to mitigate both the thermal boundary resistance and the interfacial electrostatic effects.
AI.motivation: Diamond is an attractive heat spreader for GaN electronics due to its exceptional thermal conductivity, but its integration may introduce electrostatic effects at the diamond/semiconductor interface that are often overlooked. This work aims to investigate this tradeoff and understand how diamond integration affects not only thermal performance but also the electrical characteristics of the transistor.
AI.method: The authors use Sentaurus TCAD to model AlGaN/GaN HEMTs with all-around diamond integration, incorporating advanced physical models including thermal boundary resistance (TBR) and temperature-dependent bandgap narrowing. They validate the model against experimentally reported electrothermal benefits, then observe band bending at the diamond/GaN interface. A Silvaco TCAD TLM test structure is additionally developed to characterize hole accumulation region formation.
AI.result: The simulations confirm the electrothermal benefits of diamond integration reported in experiments, but also reveal strong band bending at the diamond/GaN interface, electric field generation, and increased valence band energy in diamond. This leads to an interfacial hole accumulation region at the GaN surface that alters vertical transport and hinders current injection, preventing high on-state current.
AI.conclusion: Diamond heat spreaders improve thermal performance but can actively influence transistor electrostatics through interfacial band bending and hole accumulation. An engineered interlayer is proposed to mitigate both elevated TBR and undesired band bending, with TCAD results providing guidance for future interlayer development studies.

title: Criticality in Neural Network Function Space through Wilsonian Fixed Points and Finite-Width Corrections
comment: 30 pages, 16 figures, presented at the 3rd International Conference Mathematical Analysis and Applications in Science and Engineering (ICMASC) 2026 Conference, Portugal
summary: Neural networks can be studied not only as parameterized computational models but also as probability distributions over functions. In this paper we develop a Wilsonian interpretation of criticality in the neural network-quantum field theory correspondence, treating the infinite width Gaussian-process limit as a free field fixed point and finite width corrections as perturbations that create non-Gaussian interactions. In this way, we do not see the departure from infinite width as a small approximation error but as the process by which interaction, complexity, expressivity and phase-like behaviour enter neural network function space. Width, depth, activation nonlinearity, initialization variance, and training dynamics are considered as control parameters that change the effective action of the network ensemble. The critical regime is when the higher-order connected correlation functions become non-negligible, and when the finite width operators become relevant or marginal scaling factors, and when the function distribution becomes sensitive to scale-dependent structure. There we can view overparameterization as suppressing a relationship of interacting terms and we find that the critical structure of finite neural networks is given by finite-width effects. This framework is a theoretical basis for studying trainability, generalization, and architectural universality of neural network functions through Wilsonian fixed points, perturbations, and critical surfaces.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a Wilsonian (renormalization group) interpretation of criticality in neural networks by treating the infinite-width Gaussian process limit as a free field fixed point and finite-width corrections as perturbations introducing non-Gaussian interactions, with width, depth, activation nonlinearity, initialization variance, and training dynamics as control parameters shaping the effective action of the network ensemble.
AI.motivation: To reframe departures from the infinite-width limit not as small approximation errors but as the mechanism through which interaction, complexity, expressivity, and phase-like behavior emerge in neural network function space, providing a theoretical foundation for understanding trainability, generalization, and architectural universality.
AI.method: The approach maps the neural network-quantum field theory correspondence onto a Wilsonian renormalization group framework, where the infinite-width Gaussian process limit serves as a free-field fixed point, finite-width corrections act as perturbative operators generating non-Gaussian interactions, and control parameters (width, depth, activation nonlinearity, initialization variance, training dynamics) modify the effective action. Criticality is identified by the onset of non-negligible higher-order connected correlation functions and relevant/marginal finite-width operators.
AI.result: The framework shows that the critical structure of finite neural networks is governed by finite-width effects, where overparameterization suppresses interacting terms, and critical regimes correspond to scale-dependent sensitivity in the function distribution where finite-width operators become relevant or marginal.
AI.conclusion: The Wilsonian framework provides a principled theoretical basis for studying neural network trainability, generalization, and architectural universality through the lens of fixed points, perturbations, and critical surfaces in function space.

title: Meandering stripes in the frustrated $J_1$-$J_2$ Ising model on the honeycomb lattice
summary: We study the frustrated $J_1$-$J_2$ Ising model on the honeycomb lattice with ferromagnetic nearest-neighbor couplings fixed at $J_1=1$ and strong antiferromagnetic next-nearest-neighbor interactions, i.e., $J_2 \leq -1/4$. Little is known for this range of $J_2$, whereas for less negative values of $J_2$ the system orders ferromagnetically at low temperatures and appears to remain in the Ising universality class. In previous work it was shown that the model has a largely degenerate ground state, and it was conjectured that there is some kind of phase transition. We introduce a complex-valued nematic order parameter, which can differentiate between the high-temperature paramagnetic phase and the observed partially-disordered stripe phase at lower temperatures. Configurations in this phase consist of stripes of spins parallel with respect to one lattice direction, which collectively meander along the remaining two, producing partially disordered ground states. The sharp peaks in the specific heat observed in earlier work only appear when using periodic boundary conditions and are absent for free boundaries. Additionally, we reveal a striking dependence of the behavior on the aspect ratio of the considered samples. Ultimately, even a careful finite-size scaling analysis for $J_2 = -0.5$ and $J_2 = -1$ is unable to clearly discern between a crossover without any singularities and some form of continuous transition, including the possibility of an infinite-order transition of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) type. For $J_2=-1/4$ we find that the system remains disordered at all temperatures and that it exhibits a finite ground-state entropy per site, for which our simulations provide the accurate asymptotic estimate $S(T=0)/N = 0.230\,960\,93(14)$ in the thermodynamic limit $N\rightarrow\infty$.

AI.tldr: The paper studies the frustrated J1-J2 Ising model on the honeycomb lattice with ferromagnetic J1=1 and strong antiferromagnetic J2≤-1/4. A complex-valued nematic order parameter differentiates between the high-temperature paramagnetic phase and a partially-disordered stripe phase. The authors reveal that sharp specific heat peaks appear only with periodic boundaries, and behavior strongly depends on sample aspect ratio. Finite-size scaling analysis for J2=-0.5 and -1 cannot clearly distinguish between a crossover and some continuous transition (including possible BKT type). For J2=-1/4, the system remains disordered at all temperatures with finite ground-state entropy per site estimated as S(T=0)/N=0.23096093(14).
AI.motivation: Little is known about the strongly frustrated regime J2≤-1/4 of the J1-J2 Ising model on the honeycomb lattice, for which a largely degenerate ground state was found and a phase transition was conjectured but not characterized.
AI.method: Introduction of a complex-valued nematic order parameter to distinguish phases; computer simulations with periodic and free boundary conditions, varying sample aspect ratios, and careful finite-size scaling analysis at J2=-0.5, -1, and -1/4.
AI.result: Configurations in the low-temperature phase consist of stripe domains meandering along remaining lattice directions, producing partially-disordered ground states. Peak sharpness in specific heat depends on boundary conditions and aspect ratio. For J2=-0.5 and -1, scaling analysis cannot unambiguously distinguish crossover from continuous transition (including possible BKT). For J2=-1/4, the system remains disordered at all temperatures with ground-state entropy S(0)/N=0.23096093(14).
AI.conclusion: The nature of the phase transition in the strongly frustrated regime remains unresolved; the evidence is consistent with either a crossover without singularities, a continuous transition, or an infinite-order BKT-like transition. At the special value J2=-1/4, the model is disordered at all temperatures with a precisely estimated finite ground-state entropy per site.

title: Interband plasmons due to Mexican hat dispersion in two-dimensional materials with inverted bands
summary: Two-dimensional topological materials with Mexican-hat dispersion exhibit numerous nontrivial features, such as double-valued isoenergetic contours in k-space, strong mixing of electron and hole states, a van Hove singularity in the density of states, and specific quantum geometric properties. We find that, due to these features, Mexican-hat dispersion significantly strengthens interband plasmons, reduces their damping, and gives rise to an additional branch of the plasmon spectrum when electron-hole symmetry is broken. The plasmon spectra are limited to a finite range of the wave vector, the boundaries of which depend on the strength of the electron-electron interaction. We also reveal a relationship between the features of the plasmon spectrum and singularities of the joint density of states with a finite plasmon wave vector q, as well as features of the interband quantum metric, which also depend on q.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how two-dimensional topological materials with Mexican-hat dispersion affect interband plasmons. The Mexican-hat band structure strengthens interband plasmons, reduces their damping, and introduces an additional plasmon branch when electron-hole symmetry is broken. The plasmon spectra exist only within a finite wave-vector range determined by electron-electron interaction strength, and are linked to singularities in the joint density of states and features of the interband quantum metric, both depending on the plasmon wave vector q.
AI.motivation: To understand how the unique electronic properties of topological materials with Mexican-hat dispersion—such as double-valued isoenergetic contours, strong electron-hole mixing, van Hove singularities, and special quantum geometric properties—influence the collective excitations (plasmons) in these systems.
AI.method: The authors theoretically analyze the plasmon spectrum in two-dimensional topological materials with Mexican-hat dispersion, examining the effects of the dispersion's distinctive features (van Hove singularity, electron-hole mixing, and quantum geometry) on interband plasmon properties. They compare results under symmetric and broken electron-hole symmetry and connect plasmon features to the joint density of states and interband quantum metric as functions of q.
AI.result: Mexican-hat dispersion strengthens interband plasmons, reduces their damping, and yields an additional plasmon branch when electron-hole symmetry is broken. The plasmon spectra are restricted to a finite wave-vector range whose boundaries depend on the electron-electron interaction strength. A connection is established between plasmon spectrum features and singularities in the joint density of states, as well as features of the q-dependent interband quantum metric.
AI.conclusion: The Mexican-hat band dispersion in 2D topological materials provides a mechanism to enhance and control interband plasmons, with spectral features intimately tied to both the joint density of states and the quantum geometry of the bands. The finite wave-vector range of the plasmon spectra, tunable by electron-electron interaction, offers prospects for engineering collective excitations in these materials.

title: Electronic Toroidal Metals: Landau Theory and Magnetoelectric Fingerprints
summary: Toroidal order is a higher-rank multipolar order whose intrinsic realization in itinerant-electron systems remains unexplored. Here, we develop a generic theory of the electronic toroidal metal (ETM), in which toroidal order emerges spontaneously from electronic degrees of freedom near the Fermi surfaces. Because candidate toroidal bilinears can overlap by symmetry with the uniform charge current, we formulate a projected instability criterion that removes the noncondensable current component. Within this current-orthogonal sector, we identify a soft collective mode in the $\mathcal{P}$-odd and $\mathcal{T}$-odd particle-hole channel and demonstrate that ETM arises as a Fermi-liquid instability. We then define the toroidal moment in an itinerant system through the antisymmetric magnetoelectric response tensor. We further establish an intimate connection between this response and the topology of pseudospin texture: the rearrangement of pseudospin vortices changes the winding structure of the Fermi surfaces and markedly enhances the magnetoelectric response. ETM also exhibits characteristic nonlinear charge transport, including a pronounced enhancement of its interband quantum-geometric contribution. Our results establish ETM as a distinct metallic Landau phase and provide a general framework for understanding toroidal order generated by itinerant electrons.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a generic theory of electronic toroidal metals (ETMs), where toroidal multipolar order emerges spontaneously from itinerant electrons near Fermi surfaces, established as a Fermi-liquid instability via a current-orthogonal projected criterion, characterized by antisymmetric magnetoelectric response tied to pseudospin texture topology, and distinctive nonlinear transport.
AI.motivation: Toroidal order is a higher-rank multipolar order that has not been explored in intrinsic itinerant-electron systems; the authors aim to fill this gap by formulating a generic theoretical framework for its spontaneous emergence.
AI.method: The authors formulate a projected instability criterion that removes the noncondensable uniform charge-current component (since toroidal bilinears can overlap by symmetry with charge current), identify a soft collective mode in the P-odd and T-odd particle-hole channel, and analyze the antisymmetric magnetoelectric response tensor to define the itinerant toroidal moment. They also connect this response to pseudospin texture topology and examine nonlinear charge transport including interband quantum-geometric contributions.
AI.result: ETM arises as a Fermi-liquid instability within the current-orthogonal sector; the magnetoelectric response is intimately linked to pseudospin vortex rearrangement, which alters Fermi-surface winding structure and markedly enhances the response; ETM shows enhanced interband quantum-geometric nonlinear charge transport.
AI.conclusion: ETM is established as a distinct metallic Landau phase, providing a general framework for understanding toroidal order generated by itinerant electrons.

title: Revealing the Role of Confined Molecular H$_2$ in the Passivation of Defective Silicon Using First-Principles Simulations
summary: The passivation of silicon dangling bonds by hydrogen is a crucial requirement for silicon-based optoelectronic technology, especially for solar cells. Recent experiments on intense light soaking of silicon heterojunction solar cells unveiled interesting dynamical aspects of hydrogen passivation that are linked to Si-H bond breaking and repassivation. These processes take place predominantly in porous regions near the amorphous/crystalline interface, where hydrogen can exist in molecular form. This work addresses the question of whether molecular H$_2$ directly participates in Si-H depassivation and repassivation. Using density functional theory, we calculate and compare formation energies of point defects, multivacancy cavities and the Si(100) surface to identify relevant passivated and depassivated states. Furthermore, we employ nudged elastic band calculations to determine the activation barriers of the corresponding pathways. We find that sufficient local free volume enables a direct double-H pathway for depassivation through the formation of confined molecular H$_2$. Despite involving the breaking of two Si-H bonds, the double-H process can be energetically and kinetically competitive with the single-H process and can exhibit a reverse repassivation barrier as low as $0.15\,$eV under p-type conditions. These findings provide a plausible atomistic explanation for passivation recovery during light soaking and illuminated annealing in porous regions near amorphous/crystalline silicon interfaces.

AI.tldr: Using density functional theory and nudged elastic band calculations, this work shows that molecular H2 can directly participate in Si-H depassivation and repassivation at silicon surfaces, enabling a double-H pathway that competes with single-H processes and explains passivation dynamics during light soaking in silicon heterojunction solar cells.
AI.motivation: Understanding the dynamical aspects of hydrogen passivation—particularly Si-H bond breaking and repassivation—during light soaking of silicon heterojunction solar cells is crucial. Since these processes occur predominantly in porous regions where H2 can exist, the paper asks whether molecular H2 directly participates in depassivation/repassivation, a question not previously resolved.
AI.method: Density functional theory is used to calculate and compare formation energies of point defects, multivacancy cavities, and the Si(100) surface to identify relevant passivated and depassivated states. Nudged elastic band (NEB) calculations are employed to determine activation barriers of the corresponding reaction pathways.
AI.result: Sufficient local free volume enables a direct double-H pathway for depassivation via confined molecular H2 formation. Although it involves breaking two Si-H bonds, the double-H process can be energetically and kinetically competitive with the single-H process, and can show a reverse repassivation barrier as low as 0.15 eV under p-type conditions.
AI.conclusion: Molecular H2 can directly participate in Si-H depassivation and repassivation in porous regions near amorphous/crystalline silicon interfaces. The findings provide a plausible atomistic mechanism for passivation recovery during light soaking and illuminated annealing.

title: Time-Resolved Thermal Susceptibility Mapping via Low-Temperature Scanning Laser Microscopy
summary: We present a multiharmonic lock-in detection approach that utilizes the inverse Fast Fourier Transform to reconstruct the time evolution of thermal susceptibility with high spatial resolution. The method is implemented on a custom-built, modular scanning laser microscope designed for operation in low working-distance optical cryostats and thoroughly calibrated for spatial accuracy.
